record.paper_title: Regularity Properties of Sectorial Operators: Counterexamples and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Angles of R-sectorial operators on L^p
record.original_question: Let A be an R-sectorial operator on an L^p-space with p in (1, infinity). Must the sectorial angle omega(A) equal the R-sectorial angle omega_R(A)? The same question is asked under stronger semigroup assumptions: if -A generates an analytic C_0-semigroup, does the equality still hold when the semigroup is positive, contractive, or both positive and contractive?

evidence.quote: Problem 1. Let A be an R-sectorial operator on Lp for p ∈ (1, ∞). Does one have ω(A) = ωR(A) (if A generates a positive / contractive / positive contractive analytic C0-semigroup)?
By definition one has ω(A) ≤ ωR(A).
Definition 2.5 (R-Sectorial Operator). A sectorial operator on a Banach space X is called R-sectorial if for some ω ∈ (ω(A), π) one has R{λR(λ, A) : λ 6∈ Σω} < ∞.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a Banach space. A closed densely defined linear operator $A$ on $X$ is called sectorial if $(-\infty,0)$ is contained in the resolvent set of $A$ and $\sup_{t>0}\|t(t+A)^{-1}\|<\infty$. For a sectorial operator $A$, define the sectorial angle
$$\omega(A)=\inf\{\omega\in(0,\pi):\sigma(A)\subset\overline{\Sigma_\omega}\text{ and }\sup_{\lambda\notin\Sigma_{\omega'}}\|\lambda R(\lambda,A)\|<\infty\text{ for all }\omega'\in(\omega,\pi)\},$$
where $\Sigma_\omega=\{z\in\mathbb{C}\setminus\{0\}:|\arg z|<\omega\}$.

A family $\mathcal{T}\subset\mathcal{B}(X)$ is called $R$-bounded if there exists $C\ge 0$ such that for all $n\in\mathbb{N}$, $T_1,\dots,T_n\in\mathcal{T}$ and $x_1,\dots,x_n\in X$,
$$\Big\|\sum_{k=1}^n \varepsilon_k T_k x_k\Big\|_{L^2(\Omega;X)}\le C\Big\|\sum_{k=1}^n \varepsilon_k x_k\Big\|_{L^2(\Omega;X)},$$
where $(\varepsilon_k)$ is an i.i.d. sequence of Rademacher random variables. The $R$-bound $\mathcal{R}(\mathcal{T})$ is the smallest such $C$.

A sectorial operator $A$ is called $R$-sectorial if there exists $\omega\in(\omega(A),\pi)$ such that $\mathcal{R}\big(\{\lambda R(\lambda,A):\lambda\notin\Sigma_\omega\}\big)<\infty$. The $R$-sectorial angle $\omega_R(A)$ is the infimum of all such $\omega$. By definition $\omega(A)\le\omega_R(A)$.

Now fix $p\in(1,\infty)$ and let $X=L^p(\mu)$ for some $\sigma$-finite measure space $(\Omega,\mu)$. Let $A$ be an $R$-sectorial operator on $L^p(\mu)$.

(a) Must $\omega(A)=\omega_R(A)$?

(b) Does the equality $\omega(A)=\omega_R(A)$ hold under the additional assumption that $-A$ generates a positive analytic $C_0$-semigroup on $L^p(\mu)$?

(c) Does the equality hold when $-A$ generates a contractive analytic $C_0$-semigroup on $L^p(\mu)$?

(d) Does the equality hold when $-A$ generates an analytic $C_0$-semigroup on $L^p(\mu)$ that is simultaneously positive and contractive?
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches did not surface a published proof or counterexample for the equality of sectorial and R-sectorial angles on $L^p$, even under positivity/contractivity assumptions on the generated analytic semigroup. The problem is listed in surveys of regularity properties of sectorial operators as an open question, and no resolution appears in available literature.

status_evidence.title: Sectorial Operator - an overview | ScienceDirect Topics
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of R-sectorial operators and the angles ω(A) and ω_R(A); no general equality is asserted on Lp spaces.
status_evidence.claim: No known equality between sectorial and R-sectorial angles is established on Lp.

status_evidence.title: The Holomorphic Functional Calculus for Sectorial Operators (ISem 21)
status_evidence.snippet: Lecture notes describing sectorial and R-sectorial angles without resolving whether they coincide on Lp.
status_evidence.claim: Standard references treat the question as unresolved.
